mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand indicators (HOUST) rise by at least 5% over the prior month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be positive as market anticipates stronger sales and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following the trigger, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the prior 20d average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% suggests supply-side strength that reduces near-term uncertainty, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns do not exceed the 95th percentile of historical 60-day returns during non-expansion periods (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unionized employment (implied via UNRATE falling below 7%) creates a labor market dissonance that drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >10% AND UNRATE < 7%
failure_condition: In 5-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX 5d returns are not significantly negative (mean > -0.5%) compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a month following a negative FEDFUNDS surprise, it signals persistent inflationary pressure that drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +2% AND previous FEDFUNDS < 1.0%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than the prior 20-day average in such regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential construction (implied via GDPC1 falling for three consecutive quarters) indicates cooling demand, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as market anticipates sector rotation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change < -3% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day returns do not fall below the 10th percentile of historical 60-day returns during non-cooling quarters (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it suggests a tight labor market that pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the prior 20-day average in such regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (implied via HOUST) above trend suggests broad-based supply and demand alignment, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns do not exceed the 90th percentile of baseline 5-day returns when both proxies are above trend (regression).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS increases of at least 0.25 percentage points per month for three months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative as markets price in higher future borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > +0.25% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns do not fall below the 5th percentile of 60-day returns during non-tightening periods (quantile regression).
